title: extra•ordinary — A Book on Everyday Creativity

summary.en: Co-authored, photographed and designed a book of playful reimagined uses for ordinary objects, developed over three months of unplanned experimentation with architect friend Hisako 'Chako' Ichiki in LA. Pitched to more than ten publishers; Rockport said yes. Sold 11,000+ copies worldwide, featured in Japan's DESIGN QUARTERLY, launched via an LA gallery exhibition.
summary.jp: 建築家の友人チャコと、3 か月の思いつきの実験から生まれた本。日用品の見立て直しを写真と文章にまとめた。10 社以上に持ち込み、Rockport が刊行を決めた。世界で 1.1 万部超を売った。

creative.en: The book began with no plan and no predetermined form — three months of open-ended experimentation with a friend, only later shaped into a photographed, InDesign-designed object with a working brush as its literal spine.
creative.jp: 計画も完成形もないまま始まった本。友人との 3 か月の実験を、写真と文章にまとめてから初めて形になった。背表紙には実際に使えるブラシを綴じ込んだ。

mine: Co-authored and art-directed the entire book
Photographed every concept, setting up controlled lighting and precise compositions
Designed every layout in Adobe InDesign, building a reading rhythm that mirrors the book's message of 'look closer, look differently'
Turned an LA gallery into the book itself for the launch exhibition, building concepts as real functional pieces
Built exhibition furniture from unconventional materials
Pitched the book to more than ten publishers until Rockport Publishing said yes
team: Hisako Ichiki — architect, Bunch Design (Los Angeles) — co-developed the concept and experiments as co-author; individual contributions versus Takao's are not separated beyond 'co-author'

narrative.situation: This book began with no plan at all — a vague ambition to make something that would spark creativity in the people around them, with no idea what form it should take.

_notes: Co-authored with Hisako Ichiki; the page does not separate individual authorship contributions beyond crediting both as co-authors.
Engagement not explicitly stated; recorded as unstated rather than assumed own-venture, per the task's strict engagement rule.

cardLine.en: A book of new uses for ordinary objects. Over 11,000 copies sold.
cardLine.jp: 日常の物の、別の使い方を集めた本。1 万 1 千部超。

oneLiner.en: A book of new uses for ordinary objects.
oneLiner.jp: ありふれた物の、新しい使い方の本。

challenge.en: The book began with no plan — three months of open experimentation in Los Angeles with architect Hisako “Chako” Ichiki, reimagining everyday objects. The hard part was turning unstructured play into a printed object that asks readers to look closer, and getting a publisher to say yes to something no category fit.
challenge.jp: この本は計画なしに始まった。建築家のチャコ（Hisako Ichiki）とロサンゼルスで 3 か月、日用品の使い道を考え直す実験を続けた。難しかったのは、形のない遊びを「もっと近くで、違う目で見て」と誘う印刷物にすること。そして、どの棚にも収まらない本に、出版社の「はい」をもらうことだった。

solution.en: We co-authored it; I photographed and designed every page, pacing each spread so it asks you to pause and look again. The craft reached the spine — a working brush you can pull out and use. The decisive move was treating a mass-market book as an authored object. Rockport said yes after 10+ pitches; it sold 11,000+ copies and was featured in Japan's DESIGN QUARTERLY.
solution.jp: 共著で、私は全ページの撮影とデザインを担当した。見開きごとに「立ち止まって、もう一度見る」リズムをつくった。こだわりは背表紙にまで及ぶ。引き抜いて使える、本物のブラシだ。決め手は、量産される本を作者のいる作品として扱ったこと。10 社以上に持ち込み、Rockport が引き受けた。世界で 1.1 万部超が売れ、日本の DESIGN QUARTERLY にも載った。

role.jp: 共著・アートディレクション・デザイン
